author: sjm41
body:
* **InterPro ID / label**
IPR020830 Glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate dehydrogenase, active site

* **Example sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**
Dmel CG9467 (A0A6H2EFP4, A0A6H2EG81, Q9VH62, Q961M9)

* **Description of issue**
This entry is currently annotated with 'GO:0016620 oxidoreductase activity, acting on the aldehyde or oxo group of donors, NAD or NADP as acceptor'

The following problem was picked up by a Claude gene-review:

This is a false positive from the PROSITE GAPDH active-site pattern PS00071 ([ASV]-S-C-[NT]-T-{S}-x-[LIM]). It is an 8-residue motif, which CG9467 matches by chance as SSCTTPCM at residues 654-661, in the C-terminal region of a BTB/WD40-like KCTD3/SHKBP1-family protein. No GAPDH NAD-binding or catalytic domain is detected (no Pfam Gp_dh_N/Gp_dh_C), and InterPro's only GAPDH-related hit is the pattern entry IPR020830. UniProt's own similarity line places the protein in the KCTD3 family. A single short pattern match outside any GAPDH fold cannot support this catalytic activity. The broader oxidoreductase term rests on the same spurious hit.

So, review the contributing ProSite entry, or just remove the MF annotation?
title: InterPro2GO issue: IPR020830 Glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate dehydrogenase, active site

author: sarach06
body:
Hi Steven,
Thank you very much for this. It is indeed a false positive from the Prosite signature in this entry. A quick solution is to remove the MF annotation for now and to contact Prosite to see if they can raise the cut-off or update the model to avoid this false positive. What do you think?
Best,
Sara

author: sjm41
body:
Thanks Sara.

I did try writing to Prosite, but it seems they cannot help. I've pasted my helpdesk exchange below.
I think I'll either have to see if UP can make Dmel CG9467 a SP entry, and/or add a manual NOT annotation to 'block' the InterPro2GO annotation to Dmel CG9467.
Either way, seems that we should close this ticket as 'not planned' and I'll find another way round this?

Steven.



Hi,
The sequences you mentioned correspond to TrEmbl sequences, i.e.
sequences that are are not manually curated, as Swiss-Prot entries are,
but the result of automated annotation. As indicated in the entries
their confidence level for the annotation is poor (2/5). They have been
erroneously automatically annotated as Glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate
dehydrogenase based on the detection of the PROSITE pattern PS00071. As
Claude correctly says these PROSITE hits for the pattern PS00071
correspond to fa alse positive, i.e. a sequence that is detected by the
pattern but that do not correspond to the set of interest. This does not
change anything about the content of the rule that annotates correctly
true positives, i.e. sequences belonging to the set of interest. The
problem is that these proteins should not have been annotated according
to a false positive hit but this is the limit of automated annotation.
I hope this helps, regards,
Christian


On 10/7/2026 4:51 AM, Steven Marygold (FlyBase) via RT wrote:
Sender name: Steven Marygold
Subject: [prosite] PRU10009

Hello

PRU10009 adds an EC:1.2.1.12 (and Rhea:10300?) annotation (and maybe the 'Glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate dehydrogenase' name) to proteins matching PS00071. That, in turn, adds a GO annotation of 'GO:0004365 glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (NAD+) (phosphorylating) activity'.

However, this motif seems to appear by chance in some proteins that are not Glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate dehydrogenases.

E.g. D. melanogaster CG9467 (A0A6H2EFP4, A0A6H2EG81, Q9VH62, Q961M9) has PS00071 but there's no evidence for Glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate dehydrogenase activity.

I asked Claude about this - here's the response:

This is a false positive from the PROSITE GAPDH active-site pattern PS00071 ([ASV]-S-C-[NT]-T-{S}-x-[LIM]). It is an 8-residue motif, which CG9467 matches by chance as SSCTTPCM at residues 654-661, in the C-terminal region of a BTB/WD40-like KCTD3/SHKBP1-family protein. No GAPDH NAD-binding or catalytic domain is detected (no Pfam Gp_dh_N/Gp_dh_C), and InterPro's only GAPDH-related hit is the pattern entry IPR020830. UniProt's own similarity line places the protein in the KCTD3 family. A single short pattern match outside any GAPDH fold cannot support this catalytic activity.

So, I think PRU10009 needs to be revised to remove any 'Glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate dehydrogenase' type annotations?

Thanks.

body:
Hi Steven,

Thank you!
Sara

author: sjm41
body: I added the NOT annotations to the UP entries, so hopefully that will solve my issue. I'll close this ticket.
